summary.name: Object Animation (category: Animation Techniques). This is a supplemental design reference, not a directly named style in the source collection.
summary.visualIdentity: Everyday objects support the subject while keeping their own material, scale and contact shadows. Meaning comes from incremental movement, rotation, arrangement and replacement. Photographed poses under fixed lighting and camera are the intended medium; any digital simulation must be labelled separately.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit: playful product moments used alone; data explainers pairing with style-097 for verified quantities; music-led product promos and social loops pairing with style-105. Inferred: editorial or product pieces where objects carry meaning. Other domains are unspecified.
summary.limitations: Do not move every object together without a relationship, and do not present simulation as photography. Physics and simulated appearance are not validated. Reference numbers, scenes and aspect ratios are optional examples. Motion-021 requires real 3D and is unsuitable here. Motion-037 and 038 need actual scene assets. The source review covers only sampled seconds 1 to 8, with no audio or later scenes verified.
summary.palette: The background policy is scene_dependent, so the cream-toned tokens are illustrative, not required canvas colours. Choose backgrounds from subject, lighting and mood. Optional tokens are background #F1E9DD, foreground #3B423E and accent #8D8977; foreground on background contrast is 8.571. The accent is decorative only at 2.937. No approved exact colours are supplied, and gradients are disabled. Apply tokens only to new presentation elements, leaving object materials unchanged. The source's colour came from materials and a warm key light; its dark room and cobalt props were author choices. Recheck contrast on composited frames.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Objects hop, tilt, stack and move into cells with contact shadows, and their relationships carry meaning. Use one owner per animated property, with clear trajectories and holds at section changes. Do not add automatic springs or extra in-between poses. Exposure rate may differ from delivery frame rate. Motion-012 and 015 suit chapter and narrative steps; 037 and 038 suit real glyphs or punctuation; 021 is excluded. Interactive delivery may offer seekable playback with pause and mute; pointer and keyboard behaviour apply only there.
summary.audio: Audio is unspecified by the style, and no soundtrack is mandatory. If the brief is silent, a restrained accent on contact or placement, optional ambience, or silence for reading holds are reasonable suggestions. Music-led product pieces may schedule moves to beats only after measured audio analysis; no beat timing is supplied. Any speech needs clear space and no competing vocals.
summary.assetRequirements: No uploads are required; the brief can drive assets. Needed are photographed pose sequences or prepared layers with transparency, consistent dimensions, fixed camera and lighting, clear naming and a layer manifest. Real glyph or punctuation assets are needed only for motion-037 or 038. Use only supplied or authorised assets, and do not invent copy, brand marks or recoloured objects. Local fonts must load before rendering.
summary.combinations: Style-097 suits data meaning: objects act as verified units with labels in palette tokens, and real objects are never recoloured. Style-105 suits beat-scheduled product moves with holds at section changes. Object Animation is also listed as compatible with Kinetic Typography, Stop-Motion and many other styles. Cursor-Driven Camera Orbit fits only with real 3D. Use it alone for playful product moments.
summary.productionApproach: The style renderer uses photographed incremental poses, with Pillow for crop and size normalisation. Any digital simulation must be cached and labelled; Blender with bpy is an alternative. The motion engine is one paused GSAP timeline. HyperFrames is the default pipeline; Remotion is used only under its documented fallback condition, with the reason recorded. FFmpeg encodes sequences and audio, and chroma-js is an optional palette check. Verify forward, backward and direct seeks, and inspect decoded frames.
